body.statement: The confidence set \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is exactly equal to the result of labeled sharp-schedule inversion based on the coarsened cluster means and discrepancy \(S_N\). Cross-policy alignment of individual response labels does not change compatibility, welfare, the discrepancy, or any table probability. For a finite-instance reference algorithm, set \(d=K(n+1)|\mathcal T|\), \(B_N=\binom{C+|\mathcal T|-1}{|\mathcal T|-1}\), and \(B_H=\binom{C+d-1}{d-1}\). Precomputing the kernels and streaming over all candidate counts and all nonnegative \(d\)-cell response tables gives the explicit upper bound \(O(K|\mathcal T|n^4+(d+K^2)B_NB_H)\) exact-rational arithmetic operations, before bit-complexity costs; legality and compatibility constraints only reduce this enumeration. Here \(|\mathcal T|=\binom{n+3}{3}^{K}\), so the bound is intentionally exponential. By contrast, direct labeled-schedule enumeration ranges over as many as \(2^{2KnC}\) binary potential-outcome schedules and, for each schedule, at most \(K^C2^{nC}\) assignment points. The response-table bound is a finite quotient reference, not a polynomial-time guarantee.
body.justification: Without this quotient the exact confidence set is only a conceptual union over exponentially many labeled missing potential outcomes.
body.gap: Rigdon and Hudgens' scalar algorithm samples labeled sharp schedules, and Bazylik et al.'s exact rank computation uses a multinomial binomial-conditioning identity unavailable under two-stage exact quotas.
body.consumer: The theorem gives software authors a finite, auditable reference algorithm and a ground truth against which pruning or branch-and-bound implementations can be checked.
